Ui.Script:
-- The keyring's container id (ref MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua:1) — decision 0765. It is an -- ordinary container in every respect the seam cares about: the app feeds it like any other -- bag (its slots are the player descriptor's own 81.., no container object), and every -- container verb, the cursor, the pending-op lock and the wire drains take it unchanged. -- What makes it special is only what the reference makes special: the window's art, its -- open/close sound, and the fact that its capacity is not a wire field. KEYRING_CONTAINER = -2
-- The backpack button (MainMenuBarBackpackButton): if any bag window is open, close them -- all; otherwise open every existing bag (ref ToggleBackpack — "if numOpen > 0 then -- CloseAllBags() else OpenAllBags()"). -- -- ONE STATED DIVERGENCE from ref BackpackButton_OnClick (MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua -- l.55-69). The ref's tail re-derives the checked state from a scan of its NATIVE -- ContainerFrames — and OnShow/OnHide dispatch is SYNCHRONOUS in the reference (wow-re -- `onshow-onhide-dispatch-order.md`: Show binder 0x775750 → transition 0x76ae10 → notify -- 0x76b260 → lua_pcall, every hop a direct call), so when an addon owns the bags its -- OnShow's `SetChecked(1)` (Bagnon.lua l.33) lands FIRST and the ref tail stomps it: on -- the real client the backpack button ends UNLIT after clicking it with Bagnon, and -- lights only via the key binding (whose body is the bare `ToggleBackpack()`, no tail). -- That click-path outcome contradicts the addon's evident intent and the director's call, -- so ours swaps the scan for the auto-toggle UNDO below: checked belongs to the WINDOWS' -- OnShow/OnHide writes — ours (BenillaBagFrame_OnShow/_OnHide) and any addon's alike — -- and this handler only repairs what the CheckButton widget flipped before it ran. Every -- stock outcome is identical to the ref's (the transition writes land inside -- ToggleBackpack and are the last word); the addon case ends lit instead of stomped. -- The widget-flip UNDO itself lives in the button's XML <OnClick> wrapper — the one seat -- where the CheckButton auto-toggle has just happened — so every DIRECT caller of this -- function (the tests, a macro) gets pure toggle semantics with no checked bookkeeping -- to corrupt. function BenillaBagToggle_OnClick() -- Through the GLOBAL, so an addon that replaced `ToggleBackpack` gets the click. ToggleBackpack() end
-- ── The bag bar (decision 0216 slice 2) — four 30×30 buttons left of MainMenuBarBackpackButton, -- mirroring the reference main-bar bag buttons (CharacterBag0..3Slot). No exact reference -- XML was available to transcribe (not in the session's extracted set) — size (30×30) and -- placement (left of the backpack button) are per the brief; inter-button spacing is an -- authored assumption (2px), FLAGGED for the director's look. Each button shows the -- equipped bag's own icon (GetInventoryItemTexture, inv slots 20..23 — Bag0Slot..Bag3Slot, -- PaperDollItemFrame.dbc-verified, decision 0216 slice 2's char-feed extension) or the -- empty-slot art when no bag is equipped there. Click toggles that bag's window — NAMED -- DEFERRAL: no drag-to-equip a bag onto the bar yet (that's the paper-doll drag arc, slice -- 3's scope, not this one). -- The bag bar (and the backpack toggle) are RELOCATED onto the action bar — anchored into -- MainMenuBarArtFrame's bottom-right — which means they need seating one frame level -- above the bar art or it paints over their icons. That lever lives with the frame it's -- about: BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove (ActionBar.xml, loaded before this file), which -- carries the full explanation; the micro-button row is its second caller. Called -- nil-GUARDED here: the shipped load order always has the bar first, but ~25 bag/bank/ -- escape/merchant test harnesses load THIS file alone — and with no bar loaded there is by -- definition no bar art to seat above, so the guard's no-op is the right answer, not a -- swallowed failure.
-- Bag0Slot..Bag3Slot = live inv ids 20..23 (char_stats.rs SLOT_INFO, DBC-verified); OUR bag -- ids 1..4 map the same way (bagId N ⇒ inv slot 19+N), the id PickupInventoryItem/ -- GetInventoryItemTexture speak. function BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button) return 19 + button.bagId end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnLoad(button, bagId) button.bagId = bagId -- The button's ID is the REFERENCE's: its 1-based inventory slot, 20..23 (the real -- client gets there through PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnLoad, which resolves -- "CharacterBag0Slot" → "Bag0Slot" → GetInventorySlotInfo → 20). Nothing of ours reads -- it — every body here goes through `button.bagId` — but every ADDON does: -- `Bagnon.lua:104` computes its highlight target as `this:GetID() - 19`, and against -- an unset id that is -19, so Bagnon highlighted the wrong bag (silently, with no -- raise) on every bag-slot hover. `isBag` is the same story from the same template -- (ref BagSlotButtonTemplate OnLoad l.33), read by KeyRingItemButton_OnClick. button:SetID(19 + bagId) button.isBag = 1 button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(button) end -- Both buttons (ref BagSlotButtonTemplate inherits PaperDollItemSlotButtonTemplate, and -- its OnLoad calls PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnLoad — PaperDollFrame.lua:86 — so a bag-bar -- slot registers the pair like every doll slot; MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml:78 does the -- same for the backpack). BagSlotButton_OnClick reads no button: right-click opens the -- bag, exactly as left does. button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- Drag-to-equip (decision 0208 phase 1b's deferred bag-icon arm, now landed): the bar -- slot is a paper-doll equipment slot for bags. LEFT drag picks the equipped bag up; -- a drag/receive drops a carried bag in to equip it (PickupInventoryItem — the exact -- doll-slot transition, the app maps id 20..23 onto wire bag slots 19..22). button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") button:RegisterEvent("UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED") button:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE") button:RegisterEvent("ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) end
-- Placing/equipping a carried bag (or picking the equipped one up) rides PickupInventoryItem, -- exactly like a paper-doll slot; the empty-cursor plain click just toggles the bag's window. function BenillaBagBarSlot_Place(button) PickupInventoryItem(BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button)) BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) end
-- ref BagSlotButton_OnClick (MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.3-21): the cursor arm first (the -- ref's PutItemInBag; ours is the equip/swap PickupInventoryItem arm, decision 0208 1b), -- otherwise the toggle goes THROUGH THE GLOBAL `ToggleBag` — the exact name -- Bagnon_Core/Overrides.lua replaces — with the ref's own button sound on that arm only. -- Toggling the window directly here (what this did before) made every bag addon's override -- silently inert for the four slot buttons while the backpack button honoured it: the -- 517-line rule above ("the reference's names are the real entry points") applied to only -- one of the five buttons, and the director met the other four. function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnClick(button) if CursorHasItem() then BenillaBagBarSlot_Place(button) -- drop/equip the carried bag onto this slot else ToggleBag(button.bagId) PlaySound("BAGMENUBUTTONPRESS") end -- The click's own CheckButton auto-toggle is provisional — re-derive from the NATIVE -- window on every branch, the ref's exact tail (BagSlotButton_OnClick l.12-20 scans -- ContainerFrame1..N: SetChecked(isVisible) whether the click toggled, placed a bag, -- or did nothing). `IsBagOpen` IS that scan, under the name the reference publishes -- for it. Reading the WINDOW rather than what ToggleBag did is load-bearing both ways: -- stock, the flag is already set when the tail runs (ContainerFrame_OnShow wrote it); -- with an addon holding the bags, no ContainerFrame is shown and the slot button stays -- unlit — the reference's own behaviour, its scan being equally blind to addon frames. button:SetChecked(IsBagOpen(button.bagId) and 1 or nil) end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnEvent(button) if event == "UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED" and arg1 ~= "player" then return end -- ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED names its slot in arg1/arg2; the bar's slots are the EQUIPMENT_BAG -- space, so a bag-window lock event (a real bag id in arg1) never concerns the icon — -- repainting anyway is idempotent (the lock read below is slot-specific). BAG_UPDATE -- fires per-bag-CONTENTS change, not per-icon change (the icon is the bag ITEM's own -- texture) — repainting on it too covers the freshly-equipped-bag-template-in-flight frame. BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) end
-- ── The bar buttons' hovers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- ref GlobalStrings.lua l.132 / l.1458 (enUS), fallback form: the real localized -- GlobalStrings.lua runs before this file at runtime (ui_script/mod.rs), so these only -- fill in for the harnesses that load no patch chain. BACKPACK_TOOLTIP = BACKPACK_TOOLTIP or "Backpack" EQUIP_CONTAINER = EQUIP_CONTAINER or "Equip Container" -- ref GlobalStrings.lua l.2472 / l.2810 — the keyring's window title + button tooltip, and -- the full-keyring refusal. KEYRING = KEYRING or "Keyring" NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR = NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR or "Your keyring is full." -- **A REFERENCE TYPO, repaired here rather than lived with** (decision 1751: a divergence -- becomes faithful or becomes a record, never silent — this is the record). -- -- `PutKeyInKeyRing`'s full-ring arm reads `NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS` -- (ContainerFrame.lua l.753), and 1.12 ships **only** `NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR` -- (GlobalStrings.lua l.2810 — checked, the shorter name appears nowhere in the file). So -- in the real client the text is nil, `UIErrorsFrame:AddMessage` refuses it, and dropping -- a key onto a full keyring reports nothing at all. -- -- benilla ran its own `PutKeyInKeyRing` before 1751 and simply used the right name; now -- the reference's own file runs, so the choice is explicit. **Supplying the name the -- reference meant is the call**: the mechanism is not in dispute (its own line says which -- string it wants), nothing of Blizzard's is edited, and the alternative is a player -- gesture that silently does nothing while an error scrolls past. If fidelity to the bug -- is ever wanted instead, deleting this line is the whole change. NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS = NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS or NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR
-- Both are PLAIN tooltips — the reference calls GameTooltip:SetText here, not -- GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip, so unlike the micro buttons next door (0661) there is no second -- explanation line to be missing. They also anchor beside the button (ANCHOR_LEFT, so the -- plate opens toward screen center off a bottom-right button), NOT at the default corner. -- -- ref MainMenuBarBackpackButton OnEnter (ref-MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.91-99). The ref -- appends the live binding key with GameTooltip:AppendText; ours concatenates the same -- suffix from a LIVE GetBindingKey read since 0997, rendered through the Key Bindings -- window's display law when it is loaded. Unbound: the bare label, the ref's own read. -- The command is TOGGLEBACKPACK — the ref's own read here, and since 1494 ours too: it is -- the key that runs what a plain click on this button runs. function BenillaBagToggle_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") local text = BACKPACK_TOOLTIP local key = GetBindingKey("TOGGLEBACKPACK") if key then if KeyBindings_KeyText then key = KeyBindings_KeyText(key) end text = text .. " " .. NORMAL_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. "(" .. key .. ")" .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end GameTooltip:SetText(text, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end
-- ref BagSlotButton_OnEnter (ref-MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.86-96): the equipped bag's own -- item tooltip, or "Equip Container" for an empty slot. The ref's "(F8)".."(F11)" suffix -- needed GetBindingKey AND the TOGGLEBAG1..4 bindings; those bind as of 1494, so the ONE -- thing still missing is `GameTooltip:AppendText` — our tooltip has SetText/AddLine and no -- append verb, and the ref's suffix lands on a plate SetInventoryItem already wrote. That -- verb's byte semantics (which line does it extend?) are unverified, so the suffix waits -- rather than guessing; this is where it goes, over `GetBindingKey("TOGGLEBAG"..(5 - -- button.bagId))` — the ref's index is REVERSED against the bar, so the slot nearest the -- backpack (bagId 1) is TOGGLEBAG4/F11 and the farthest (bagId 4) is TOGGLEBAG1/F8. function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") if not GameTooltip:SetInventoryItem("player", BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button)) then GameTooltip:SetText(EQUIP_CONTAINER, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end end
-- `BagSlotButton_OnEnter()` — THE REFERENCE'S NAME for the hover above, and the entry point -- the four `CharacterBag<N>Slot` buttons actually call (their XML below). Published for the -- same standing reason `ToggleBackpack` is: an addon replaces the client's global and -- expects the client to call the replacement. -- -- `Bagnon.lua:67` is the exact shape, and it is a hover-frequency call, not a rare one: -- bBagSlotButton_OnEnter = BagSlotButton_OnEnter -- capture ours -- BagSlotButton_OnEnter = BagnonBlizBag_OnEnter -- replace the global -- Bagnon's replacement highlights the matching slots in its own window and then calls the -- capture. With the global absent that capture was nil, and — because nothing here ever -- looked the global up — the replacement was never reached to raise on it: Bagnon's -- highlight was simply, silently inert. Corpus demand is exactly one addon (this one) at -- two sites; its siblings `BagSlotButton_OnClick`/`_OnDrag`/`_OnShiftClick`/ -- `BackpackButton_OnClick` score ZERO and are deliberately not published (1210). -- -- The reference's body takes no argument and reads `this`; so does this one. function BagSlotButton_OnEnter() BenillaBagBarSlot_OnEnter(this) end
-- ref BagSlotButton_OnClick / _OnDrag / _OnShiftClick (MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.3-53), -- published beside _OnEnter above for the same reason it was: they are the names -- BagSlotButtonTemplate binds, and an addon that builds its bag bar from that template -- reaches them and nothing else. pfUI is the measured caller (modules/bags.lua l.537), and -- it CHAINS them — `GetScript("OnEnter")` then calling what it got — so a missing one is -- not a dead button, it is a nil call inside the addon's own wrapper. -- -- **Our four bar slots do not come through here** and are untouched: they carry an explicit -- bagId from BenillaBagBarSlot_OnLoad and wire the Benilla bodies directly. These three -- exist so a TEMPLATE-built button reaches the same bodies — one implementation, two entry -- points, which is the whole point of publishing the reference's name over ours. -- -- NOT the reference's bodies, and ONE of the two reasons for that expired with decision -- 1751's bag swap. The reference's versions do two things: scan -- ContainerFrame1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES to re-derive the checked state — which now works -- here, and the tails below do exactly it through `IsBagOpen` — and reach for -- `PutItemInBag` / `PickupBagFromSlot`, which this client still does not bind (our -- equip/swap arm is the paper doll's `PickupInventoryItem`, 0208 1b). That second half is -- what still keeps `Interface\FrameXML\MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml` out of the manifest: -- sourcing it today hands every caller a body that raises on a verb we have not built. -- Those two verbs are the bag BAR's migration ticket, and this file is what it replaces. function BagSlotButton_OnClick() BenillaBagBarSlot_OnClick(this) end
-- The drag arm: ref picks the equipped bag up with PickupBagFromSlot; ours is the same -- PickupInventoryItem transition the bar slots already use, so an empty cursor picks the -- bag up and a held bag places it. function BagSlotButton_OnDrag() BenillaBagBarSlot_Place(this) end
-- Shift-click opens every bag if this slot HOLDS one (ref l.38-41 verbatim), then re-reads -- the checked state off our own window the way BenillaBagBarSlot_OnClick's tail does. function BagSlotButton_OnShiftClick() if GetInventoryItemTexture("player", this:GetID()) then OpenAllBags() end this:SetChecked(this.bagId and IsBagOpen(this.bagId) and 1 or nil) end
-- ref OnLeave for both (l.100-102 / the template's own): a plain Hide, no fade — the item -- half of the split BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave's comment describes. function BenillaBagBarButton_OnLeave() if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end end
-- ref KeyRingButton's OnLoad/OnClick/OnReceiveDrag (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.142-199). -- The button is authored HIDDEN and only ever revealed by MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing -- (ActionBar.xml), which is where the whole show/hide law and its divergence note live. function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnLoad(button) button:SetID(KEYRING_CONTAINER) button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") -- The ref watches PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD / VARIABLES_LOADED / BAG_UPDATE on the bar's art -- frame; with no saved variable there is nothing for VARIABLES_LOADED to restore, and -- BAG_UPDATE is what actually carries "a key just arrived". button:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") button:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(button) end BenillaKeyRingButton_OnEvent() end
function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnEvent() if MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing then MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing() end end
function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnClick(button) -- Holding something ⇒ file it; empty-handed ⇒ open/close the keyring (ref l.166-173). if CursorHasItem() then PutKeyInKeyRing() else ToggleKeyRing() end -- Re-derive the lit ring from the window, the same provisional-toggle tail every other -- bag-bar button uses. The keyring's window is an ordinary ContainerFrame now, so this -- is the same `IsBagOpen` scan as the four bag slots', at KEYRING_CONTAINER. button:SetChecked(IsBagOpen(KEYRING_CONTAINER) and 1 or nil) end
-- ref l.180-184: the plain KEYRING title plus the ref's own empty AddLine (which reserves -- the second row the binding key would print into — we ship no TOGGLEKEYRING binding, the -- same gap the bag slots' "(F1)".."(F4)" suffixes have). function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") GameTooltip:SetText(KEYRING, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) local invSlot = BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button) local texture = GetInventoryItemTexture("player", invSlot) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or "Interface\\PaperDoll\\UI-PaperDoll-Slot-Bag") -- Dim while the bag is up on the cursor or a pending equip is in flight (the doll's own -- drag feedback, IsInventoryItemLocked — the bag-slot twin of BenillaBagSlot_Update). if IsInventoryItemLocked(invSlot) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) elseif button:IsEnabled() ~= 0 then button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) else -- Disabled by Disable_BagButtons below: keep the grey. The reference needs no such -- arm — its desaturation is a shader flag on the texture, untouched by an Update -- that only re-sets the image — but ours IS a vertex colour (UiPanels.xml -- SetDesaturation), so a bag update behind the open game menu would otherwise -- repaint the icon bright under a button that stayed dead. button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 0.5) end end
-- ── The item-push drop animation (decision 0887) ───────────────────────────────────────── -- An item lands in a bag: its icon pops in above the bag bar, hangs there, then falls into -- the button that took it and shrinks away. ref ItemAnim (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.4-16 + -- .lua l.68-80, .lua l.92-94): each bag button owns a hidden child that, on ITEM_PUSH -- naming its own container, swaps in the pushed item's icon, rewinds to sequence time 0 and -- shows itself; OnAnimFinished hides it again. A second push on the same button RESTARTS it -- (SetSequenceTime(0,0)); pushes into different bags run independently. That is exactly the -- machine below, with the reference's ITEM_PUSH `arg1` translated from its inventory-slot -- vocabulary (20..23) into ours (bagId 1..4) app-side — ui_loot.rs `push_container` carries -- the byte-verified selector. -- -- The reference's is a <Model> playing Interface\ItemAnimations\ForcedBackpackItem.mdx — a -- single 4-vertex quad on one animated bone, i.e. a 2D icon card with keyframed scale, alpha -- and offset. benilla has no Model widget (decision 0137's Cooldown took the same posture: -- model the mechanism, let our own renderer draw it), so it is a Texture driven by the -- model's OWN tracks, read out of the shipped .m2 with `benilla-extract m2anim`/`m2bones`: -- -- sequence 0, CLAMP (plays once), duration 1.000 s -- texture-weight (alpha) 0.000→0.0 0.133→1.0 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.0 linear -- bone 0 scale 0.000→1.0 0.133→1.2 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.014 linear -- bone 0 translation 0.000→(0,0) 0.500→(0,0) 1.000→(+0.010,-0.040) -- the quad itself: 0.03 x 0.03 model units, blend Alpha, unlit, no depth write -- -- So: fade in over the first 133 ms while swelling to 1.2x; settle back to full size by -- 267 ms; from there dwindle and fade continuously for the remaining 733 ms — while the -- POSITION holds until the half-second and only then falls. The three tracks deliberately -- do not share a schedule: the card is already down to ~0.69 size and ~0.68 alpha when it -- starts moving, so the drop reads as the icon being drawn into the bag rather than as a -- solid tile sliding. Those numbers are the file's, not ours. -- -- THE MODEL-UNIT → PIXEL SCALE is no longer ours to calibrate: the <Model> widget's -- projection is RE-recorded now (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-animation-clock.md`, -- dispatched over the pet bar's B228 and folded back with it). The ortho leg gives -- -- px per model unit = (5/3) * modelScale * layoutScale * screenHeightPx -- -- which in FrameXML units is **1280 * modelScale * layoutScale**, aspect- and -- resolution-independent, with the model ORIGIN at the frame rect's bottom-left. The ref's -- `ItemAnimTemplate` (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml:4) carries **no `scale` attribute**, so -- modelScale is 1 and the constant is a flat 1280. Decision 0887's named gap is closed. -- -- This REPLACES a back-fit, and the back-fit is worth naming because it looked like -- evidence. The old 1200 came from assuming CooldownFrameTemplate's 0.04-unit sweep -- *exactly* covers a 36 px action button at its scale="0.75" (⇒ K = 1200). The assumption -- is the error: at the real projection that sweep is 0.04 · 1280 · 0.75 = **38.4 px**, so -- it overhangs its button by 6.7% rather than fitting it — exactly as the autocast shine's -- 30.72 px square overhangs its 30 px button. Solving against a wrong premise produced a -- number that then "cross-checked" against a second model derived the same wrong way, and -- both files cited the agreement as the reason to trust it. -- -- Everything below is the model's own ratios times this constant, so the correction lands -- in one place and the animation stays in proportion. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT = 1280 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION = 1.0
-- ── The widget rect, and why the card is not placed against the button ───────────────── -- A `<Model>` with no `<Size>` and no `setAllPoints` takes its rect from the **M2 header -- bounding box** (`MD20+0xB4`, max−min per axis), consumed RAW as layout units — unlike -- CSimpleTexture's texel fallback, there is no AbsDimension conversion. So the ref's -- ItemAnim widget is **42.41 x 124.72**, nothing like the 36-square everyone assumes from -- looking at the XML, and **model-space (0,0,0) lands on that rect's BOTTOM-LEFT corner**. -- (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-implicit-size-law.md`, §5-cross-checked: vtable -- 0x81c5d8 +0x1c/+0x20 -> 0x76d080/0x76d0d0, bbox source 0x713640 at `713661 add esi,0xb4`. -- The one worker who read `MD20+0xD0` — the VertexBox — got an all-zero box and concluded -- the widget was degenerate; that wrong premise is exactly what the pair round exists to -- catch, and it is why this looked unresolvable in 0887.) -- -- That rect is the whole reason this animation reads the way it does: it stands 124.72 tall -- off the button's own bottom edge, so the card's travel band reaches **54 px above the -- button's top**. Decision 0887 could not know that and placed the card against the -- button's CENTER instead, which is what put it in the wrong place in x and gave it no -- horizontal drift at all. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_W = 42.41 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_H = 124.72 -- Where that rect hangs off the button: the ref anchors the widget's BOTTOMRIGHT to the -- button's, 10 in from the right for the five bag buttons and flush (0) for the keyring — -- MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.19-27 (BagSlotButtonTemplate) and l.152-160 (KeyRingButton). -- Per-button, so it is an OnLoad argument, not a constant. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ANCHOR_X = -10
-- ── The model's own numbers, unrounded ──────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Every one of these was rounded in 0887 and every rounding moved the card. The quad span -- read as 0.03 (it is 0.0288 — a 4% size error), and the translation as (0.010, -0.040) -- (which alone accounts for half a pixel of the landing point). -- -- The bone transform is `v' = pivot + T(t) + S(t) * (v - pivot)` — three wow-re workers -- derived that independently in three matrix conventions and agreed. The pivot -- (M2CompBone+0x60) is NOT the quad's centre: it sits 0.23 px right and 0.07 px above it, -- so the card shrinks *almost* in place and drifts a fifth of a pixel doing it. Keeping -- the pivot as its own term rather than folding it into the centre is what makes this -- reproduce the reference exactly at all three sampled times instead of nearly. -- Bone 0's ROTATION track is empty (nKeys = 0), so there is no roll to model. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X = 0.017580900341272354 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y = 0.053958501666784286 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_X = 0.017400000942870975 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_Y = 0.053900001570582390 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_SPAN = 0.028800001833587885
-- {time, value} keyframes, linear between (M2 track interpolation 1) — the file's own keys, -- at full precision. The three tracks keep DIFFERENT schedules and that is the whole feel: -- the card fades up while swelling to 1.2x over 133 ms, settles back to full size at -- 267 ms, then dwindles and fades *continuously* for the remaining 733 ms — while its -- position holds until the half second and only then falls. So it is already at ~0.69 size -- and ~0.68 alpha when it starts to move, and it is invisible by the time it lands. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.133, 1.0}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.0} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE = { {0.000, 1.0}, {0.133, 1.2000000476837158}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.01441549975425005} } -- Translation is per-AXIS: the card falls 51.4 px and drifts 13.3 px RIGHT, so one shared -- 0..1 "drop" curve (0887's shape) cannot express it — the old code had no horizontal term -- at all and moved the card the wrong way in x when it inferred one. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_X = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, 0.010394600220024586} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_Y = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, -0.040167398750782013} }
-- Sample a {time, value} keyframe list at `t`, linear between keys, clamped at both ends -- (the M2 sampler's own shape for a CLAMP sequence). function BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(track, t) local last = table.getn(track) if t <= track[1][1] then return track[1][2] end for i = 2, last do local key = track[i] if t <= key[1] then local prev = track[i - 1] local span = key[1] - prev[1] if span <= 0 then return key[2] end return prev[2] + (key[2] - prev[2]) * (t - prev[1]) / span end end return track[last][2] end
-- Place/size/fade the card for the current clock, from the model's own transform. -- -- The card's centre in MODEL space is `pivot + T(t) + S(t)*(quadCentre - pivot)`; times the -- projection constant that is its offset in layout units from the model origin, which is -- the widget rect's bottom-left corner. The rect's own BOTTOMRIGHT hangs off the button's, -- so the card is placed against the BUTTON'S BOTTOMRIGHT — never its centre — and the -- frame width is what converts between the two. -- -- On screen: a button-sized card appears with its bottom edge ~13.6 px ABOVE the button's -- top, pops to 1.2x and back while fading in, hangs there through the first half second, -- then falls down-and-right INTO the button, shrinking to a half-pixel point at its centre -- as it fades out. Reproduces the reference at t = 0, 0.133 and 1.0 to the hundredth of a -- pixel (`modelframe-implicit-size-law.md` §3's table). -- -- NOT modelled, deliberately, and both are named in the record: the reference's widget -- CLIPS the card to its own rect, which shaves 1.94 px off the right edge at the 1.2x peak -- **at 4:3 only** (16:10 and 16:9 clear it); and the widget clears the depth buffer inside -- that 124.72-tall rect every paint. benilla draws this as a Texture, not a Model, so it -- inherits neither — reproducing an aspect-conditional sliver would be hard-coding a -- rendering artefact rather than modelling the mechanism that causes it. function BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) local t = anim.elapsed local k = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT local scale = BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE, t) local size = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_SPAN * scale * k local cx = (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X + BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_X, t) + scale * (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_X - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X)) * k local cy = (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y + BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_Y, t) + scale * (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_Y - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y)) * k anim:SetWidth(size) anim:SetHeight(size) anim:SetPoint("CENTER", anim:GetParent(), "BOTTOMRIGHT", anim.anchorX - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_W + cx, cy) anim:SetAlpha(BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA, t)) end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnLoad (l.68-70): the card listens for ITEM_PUSH and nothing else. It is -- authored hidden, so it costs no OnUpdate until a push shows it (events reach hidden -- frames; OnUpdate does not — the reference's own split). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnLoad(anim, containerId, anchorX) anim.containerId = containerId -- The widget's own offset from the button's BOTTOMRIGHT: -10 for the five bag buttons, -- flush 0 for the keyring (the ref's two different anchors — see the constant block). anim.anchorX = anchorX or BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ANCHOR_X anim.icon = getglobal(anim:GetName() .. "Icon") anim.elapsed = 0 anim:RegisterEvent("ITEM_PUSH") end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnEvent (l.72-80): `if this:GetParent():GetID() == arg1`, then -- ReplaceIconTexture(arg2) / SetSequence(0) / SetSequenceTime(0,0) / Show. A push into a bag -- with no button (a bank bag) matches nothing and animates nowhere, there and here. function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnEvent(anim) if arg1 ~= anim.containerId then return end anim.icon:SetTexture(arg2) anim.elapsed = 0 -- Seat the card above its button rather than at load: the bag bar's own level is set in -- the BUTTON's OnLoad (BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove), which the loader may run after -- this child exists. Re-deriving it per push is one call and can never read it stale. anim:SetFrameLevel(anim:GetParent():GetFrameLevel() + 1) BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) anim:Show() end
-- The CLAMP sequence's end is the ref's OnAnimFinished → this:Hide() (l.92-94). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnUpdate(anim, elapsed) anim.elapsed = anim.elapsed + (elapsed or 0) if anim.elapsed >= BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION then anim:Hide() return end BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) end
-- The bag BAR's five buttons (the backpack toggle + the four equipped-bag slots) — the row -- Disable_/Enable_BagButtons greys as a unit. Distinct from UiPanels.xml's BAG_WINDOWS, -- which is the five bag *windows* those buttons open. BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS = { "MainMenuBarBackpackButton", "CharacterBag0Slot", "CharacterBag1Slot", "CharacterBag2Slot", "CharacterBag3Slot" }
-- Disable_BagButtons / Enable_BagButtons — ref MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.102-128, called -- by GameMenuFrame's OnShow/OnHide (decision 0674) and by nothing else: while the game menu -- holds the screen, the whole bag row greys out. That is the *visible* half of a rule the -- panel manager already enforces (ShowUIPanel's native-center gate refuses every window -- while the menu is up — UiPanels.xml `CanOpenPanels`); without it the bags would look -- clickable and simply do nothing. -- -- Mapping onto benilla's row: the ref's MainMenuBarBackpackButton is MainMenuBarBackpackButton and -- CharacterBag0..3Slot are CharacterBag0Slot..4 — and in BOTH cases the greying goes onto -- the button's `$parentIcon` LAYER texture, never onto a state texture. That is the -- reference's own structure and it is load-bearing here: a disabled button draws its -- DisabledTexture, and with none set it draws no state texture at all -- (`ButtonState::region_visible`), so greying a NormalTexture would grey something already -- gone. The four slots' UI-Quickslot2 rings ARE state textures and do vanish while -- disabled unless the slot states one explicitly — so what you should see is the -- ring stay put and the bag icon grey — which is why each slot repeats its ring as -- DisabledTexture (see the slot instances below). function Disable_BagButtons() for _, button in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS) do local b = getglobal(button) b:Disable() SetDesaturation(b.icon, 1) end end
function Enable_BagButtons() for _, button in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS) do local b = getglobal(button) b:Enable() SetDesaturation(b.icon, nil) end -- The four slots' own paint decides their restored colour: an item locked on the cursor -- wants its 0.4 grey back, which the un-desaturate above does not restore (it clears -- the greyscale flag, not the tint). for i = 1, 4 do BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(getglobal("CharacterBag" .. (i - 1) .. "Slot")) end end

Scripts.OnLoad: self.icon = getglobal("MainMenuBarBackpackButtonIconTexture") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(self) end
Scripts.OnClick: self:SetChecked(not self:GetChecked()) if IsShiftKeyDown() then OpenAllBags() else BenillaBagToggle_OnClick() end
